editorialNote: Profiles are curated and source-linked. Live mentions are updated from Quantum Live. Company claims and future targets are attributed; no cross-platform performance ranking is implied.

companies.name: IBM
companies.tagline: Superconducting systems. An open software ecosystem.
companies.description: Builds superconducting quantum processors and the Qiskit software stack, with research spanning error correction, algorithms, and quantum–classical workflows.

achievement.title: Direct control over quantum execution
achievement.summary: IBM describes client-side control of error-mitigation and correction workflows through its directed execution model.

developments.title: IBM Quantum’s Q3 platform update
developments.summary: Updates cover Nighthawk r2 access, mitigation tools, and Qiskit interfaces beyond Python.

companies.name: Google Quantum AI
companies.tagline: Error-corrected computing, one logical step at a time.
companies.description: Develops superconducting processors and quantum error-correction methods, including Willow, alongside algorithms and experimental quantum simulation.

achievement.title: Below-threshold error correction with Willow
achievement.summary: Google reported that increasing the size of an error-correcting code reduced logical errors on Willow.

developments.title: Magic-state cultivation on Willow
developments.summary: Google reports a hardware demonstration of magic-state cultivation, with results published in Science. Larger-scale fault tolerance remains an engineering goal.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.tagline: Topological-device research meets a quantum cloud ecosystem.
companies.description: Investigates semiconductor–superconductor devices for topological quantum computing and develops Azure Quantum tools for quantum and classical research workflows.

achievement.title: Majorana device research and Azure Quantum
achievement.summary: Combines a topological-device research program with a cloud and software ecosystem. Device claims should be assessed alongside the underlying technical research.

developments.title: Microsoft describes its Majorana 2 approach
developments.summary: Microsoft reports a changed material stack and longer-lived device states. Its 2029 scalable-system date is a company target, not a delivered machine.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.tagline: The classical compute layer around quantum machines.
companies.description: Builds GPU-accelerated simulation, hybrid programming, interconnect, and AI tools through cuQuantum, CUDA-Q, NVQLink, and Ising. It supports quantum hardware builders rather than supplying its own qubit platform.

achievement.title: NVQLink connects quantum and accelerated computing
achievement.summary: Introduced an architecture for coupling quantum processors to GPUs for control, decoding, and hybrid applications.

developments.title: Ising models for quantum calibration and decoding
developments.summary: NVIDIA announced open AI models for processor calibration and error-correction decoding, complementing CUDA-Q and NVQLink.

companies.name: IonQ
companies.description: Develops trapped-ion quantum computers and networking technologies, with research into processor interconnects and architectures for fault-tolerant computation.

achievement.title: Interconnecting trapped-ion quantum systems
achievement.summary: IonQ reports entanglement-related photonic links between two independent commercial trapped-ion systems in a joint project with AFRL.

developments.title: Walking Cat fault-tolerance architecture
developments.summary: A proposed trapped-ion architecture describes how error correction and ion transport could support a larger fault-tolerant computer.

companies.name: Quantinuum
companies.tagline: Trapped-ion hardware with a full quantum software stack.
companies.description: Develops trapped-ion quantum processors and integrated software for hybrid programs, error correction, and scientific applications. Its Helios system builds on a quantum charge-coupled-device approach.

achievement.title: Commercial introduction of Helios
achievement.summary: Quantinuum introduced Helios with real-time classical control and Guppy, a language for combining quantum and classical operations.

developments.title: Hybrid-compute collaboration with Oracle
developments.summary: Quantinuum and Oracle announced work to integrate quantum and classical computing through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.

companies.name: Rigetti
companies.tagline: Superconducting processors built from connected chiplets.
companies.description: Builds superconducting quantum processors, modular chiplet architectures, and Quantum Cloud Services, with an emphasis on control, fidelity, and system scaling.

achievement.title: Cepheus-1-108Q becomes generally available
achievement.summary: Rigetti announced a 108-physical-qubit system assembled from twelve interconnected nine-qubit chiplets, accessible through QCS and Amazon Braket.

developments.title: 108-qubit system deployment update
developments.summary: The announcement describes the modular architecture and reports gate-performance figures. Physical-qubit count alone is not a measure of useful computational advantage.

companies.name: D-Wave
companies.tagline: Quantum annealing, with an expanding gate-model program.
companies.description: Develops quantum annealing systems and hybrid solvers for optimization. Its acquisition of Quantum Circuits adds a superconducting gate-model development program.

achievement.title: Annealing and gate-model technology under one roof
achievement.summary: D-Wave completed its acquisition of Quantum Circuits, adding an error-detecting superconducting gate-model approach alongside its annealing business.

developments.title: A dual-platform development strategy
developments.summary: The acquisition announcement outlines gate-model plans. Future delivery dates and projected error-correction performance remain company roadmap statements.

companies.name: PsiQuantum
companies.tagline: Silicon photonics and a path through semiconductor manufacturing.
companies.description: Develops photonic quantum computing using the Omega silicon-photonics platform, optical networking, and the Construct suite for fault-tolerant algorithm design.

achievement.title: Omega photonics platform
achievement.summary: Integrates photon sources, detectors, and switches in a foundry-based platform. Planned utility-scale systems require further integration and validation.

developments.title: Construct collaboration with Brookhaven Lab
developments.summary: The partners announced work on algorithms and scientific applications using Construct for future fault-tolerant computers.

companies.name: QuEra
companies.tagline: Reconfigurable atoms, analog simulation, and logical-qubit research.
companies.description: Develops neutral-atom processors using optical control and Rydberg interactions, from Aquila’s analog simulations to research into error-corrected quantum computing.

achievement.title: Aquila and a neutral-atom roadmap
achievement.summary: Aquila provides access to analog neutral-atom simulation. Logical-qubit research supports a separate path toward fault-tolerant operation.

developments.title: Fault-tolerant systems roadmap
developments.summary: QuEra describes a 2028–2029 roadmap beyond Libra and invites application co-design. The dates and capabilities are targets, not completed deployments.
